title: Scissor car jack
description: A pressed-steel scissor jack sized after jacks sold as 1 t: four U-section arms with gear-tooth ends, a screw between a nut trunnion and a bearing trunnion, a saddle held level by the gears, and a tilted folding crank on a Hooke joint.

difficulty.rationale: A closed rhombus with screw and gear couplings plus a spherical Hooke loop, four sheet-metal arm configurations with involute teeth, process and motion checks, and kernel limits to work around.

standards: EN 1494 (mobile jacks; scope and contents read only, no requirement or value; no compliance claimed)
materials: Cold-rolled steel 3 mm, safety-yellow powder coat
Steel screw and trunnions, bright zinc
Black-painted crank on a Hooke joint with a zinc-plated cross, rubber grip and saddle pad

motion.cycle: there and back: the screw turns from the lowest position to the highest and back

contacts.why: the thread is the joint: the nut's bore is the tap drill and the screw is at the major diameter (F-014)
the headed pin is pressed into the nut trunnion's blind hole, a drawn line-on-line press fit
the headed pin is pressed into the bearing trunnion's blind hole, a drawn line-on-line press fit
the rubber pad is bonded to the saddle's top face

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Passed the Acceptance on the numbers: 0 dof, saddle 121.9 to 378.0 mm against the rhombus to 1e-9 mm, level to 6e-15°, span to 1.4e-10 mm, handle 17.6 mm above the ground, no dead point, 73 samples. It had to guess many sizes (arm section, module, crank tilt), so the arms' sizes and teeth, the crank and the friction were added to the prompt afterwards; that wording was not retested. The Hooke closed form held only modulo pi over 67.5 turns in that rebuild.
